_about: Plain-language labels for the oncologist report (scripts/build_report.py). Written by a senior heme-onc agent from rubric_v2.toml, case.toml and gold.json, then checked item by item against the rubric text by an independent heme-onc agent (2026-10-22). Not human-reviewed. Never shown to the model.

case_card.title: Stage IV DLBCL with kidney-adrenal involvement and rising creatinine
case_card.patient: 67M with 6 wk epigastric/LUQ pain, drenching night sweats and 8 kg weight loss; ECOG 2, T2DM on metformin, taking ibuprofen 400 mg QID. PET-CT: 9.4 cm retroperitoneal/mesenteric mass plus FDG-avid R kidney, L adrenal and liver lesions; GCB DLBCL (MYC 20%, BCL2 30%, FISH negative), marrow negative, LDH 1,290, uric acid 10.4, creatinine 1.1 -> 1.5.
tests: Kidney, adrenal and liver lesions are extranodal organ disease, so stage IV, IPI 5/5 and CNS-IPI 6/6.
MYC 20% / BCL2 30% with negative FISH: neither double-expressor nor double-hit, so no intensified regimen such as DA-EPOCH-R.
ECOG 2 is disease-related in a patient who wants cure: full-dose Pola-R-CHP (or R-CHOP) x6 after a steroid prephase, not mini-CHOP or palliation.
Uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN and rising creatinine mean high TLS risk: IV hydration, rasburicase after G6PD check, TLS labs every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours, stop NSAIDs.
High CNS risk: MRI brain and LP with CSF cytology/flow now; HD-MTX only as an individualized option once renal function recovers and NSAIDs are stopped.
case_card.correct_plan: Curative full-dose Pola-R-CHP x6 (R-CHOP acceptable) after a 5-7 day prednisone 100 mg prephase, with admission for TLS prophylaxis (IV fluids, rasburicase after G6PD, TLS labs q6-12h), stopping ibuprofen, pegfilgrastim every cycle and a steroid glucose plan. Baseline MRI brain and LP; HD-MTX prophylaxis individualized and deferred until renal recovery; end-of-treatment PET-CT read by Lugano/Deauville.

items.label: Diagnoses DLBCL, NOS, germinal-center B-cell (GCB) subtype
items.why: CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1- biopsy defines GCB DLBCL; correct diagnosis anchors regimen choice and prognosis.

items.label: Stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage IV
items.why: Kidney, adrenal and liver organ involvement make this stage IV; it drives IPI, CNS risk and treatment intensity.

items.label: Attributes stage IV to kidney, adrenal and liver involvement
items.why: Naming these extranodal organs shows the stage is earned correctly and flags the kidney/adrenal CNS-risk sites.

items.label: Notes B symptoms (night sweats, weight loss or fevers)
items.why: Drenching sweats and ~10% weight loss confirm stage IVB and active, symptomatic disease needing prompt treatment.

items.label: Stages the disease below IV (stage I, II or III)
items.why: Understaging ignores organ involvement, underestimates IPI and CNS risk, and could lead to undertreatment.

items.label: States not double-expressor (MYC 20%, BCL2 30%) nor double-hit (FISH negative)
items.why: Below-threshold IHC and negative FISH mean standard Pola-R-CHP/R-CHOP applies, not an intensified high-grade approach.

items.label: Calls this double-hit lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
items.why: FISH is negative; mislabelling as double-hit would push toward unnecessary, more toxic intensified chemotherapy.

items.label: Calls this lymphoma double-expressor
items.why: MYC 20% and BCL2 30% are below thresholds; the label misstates prognosis and may prompt escalation.

items.label: Calculates IPI 5 (or high-risk IPI 4-5)
items.why: Age >60, high LDH, ECOG 2, stage IV and multiple extranodal sites; supports Pola-R-CHP and close monitoring.

items.label: Calculates CNS-IPI 6 or high risk, counting kidney/adrenal involvement
items.why: Kidney/adrenal disease plus IPI factors give roughly 10-12% CNS relapse risk, mandating CNS staging and a prophylaxis discussion.

items.label: Recommends curative full-dose Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP for 6 cycles
items.why: Fit-for-cure patient with high-risk disease; six full-dose cycles offer the best chance of cure.

items.label: Names Pola-R-CHP as preferred given IPI >=2 (R-CHOP acceptable)
items.why: He meets POLARIX eligibility; Pola-R-CHP improved progression-free survival over R-CHOP in IPI >=2 disease.

items.label: Recommends steroid prephase (prednisone ~100 mg, 5-7 days) before cycle 1
items.why: Age >60, ECOG 2 and high tumor burden: prephase lowers first-cycle toxicity and often improves performance status.
items.checker_revised: The why calls the disease 'bulky', but the largest mass is 9.4 cm, which the reference plan says is just under the 10 cm Lugano bulk cut-off. The rubric text says 'high tumor burden', so the why should say that too.

items.label: Recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care or hospice
items.why: Denies a curable lymphoma to a patient whose stated goal is cure and whose ECOG 2 is disease-driven.

items.label: Recommends DA-EPOCH-R or another intensified regimen
items.why: Not double-hit or double-expressor; intensified therapy adds toxicity, especially with renal impairment, without proven benefit here.

items.label: Starts with a dose-reduced regimen such as R-mini-CHOP
items.why: At 67 with disease-related ECOG 2, attenuated dosing needlessly compromises the chance of cure.

items.label: Identifies high CNS-relapse risk from kidney/adrenal involvement and CNS-IPI
items.why: Recognising this risk triggers baseline CNS staging and an informed prophylaxis discussion before treatment starts.

items.label: Orders contrast MRI brain and LP with CSF cytology and flow
items.why: Occult CNS disease must be excluded now; finding it would change the regimen entirely.

items.label: Discusses CNS prophylaxis (e.g. HD-MTX) as individualized, tied to renal function/NSAIDs
items.why: Benefit is uncertain, and HD-MTX is unsafe with creatinine 1.5, renal involvement and ongoing ibuprofen.

items.label: Schedules HD-MTX now (e.g. with cycle 1) ignoring rising creatinine/NSAIDs
items.why: Methotrexate with falling eGFR, renal lymphoma and NSAIDs risks severe nephrotoxicity and delayed clearance.

items.label: Plans end-of-treatment PET-CT read by Lugano/Deauville 5-point scale
items.why: Standard way to confirm complete metabolic response and decide whether further therapy is needed.

items.label: Biopsies residual Deauville 4-5 uptake if it would change management
items.why: PET-positive residual masses can be false positives; tissue confirmation avoids unnecessary salvage therapy.

items.label: Recognises high TLS risk; orders IV hydration, a urate-lowering drug and TLS labs every 6-12 hours
items.why: Uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN and rising creatinine: cycle 1 could precipitate renal failure or arrhythmia. At this risk TLS labs are checked every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours; once-daily checks do not meet the requirement.

parts.label: States the TLS risk is high (or orders TLS prophylaxis)
TLS labs every few hours (e.g. every 6-12 h), not daily

items.label: Favors rasburicase for hyperuricemia with renal impairment, checking G6PD first
items.why: Rasburicase lowers urate rapidly to protect the kidneys; G6PD deficiency risks hemolysis and methemoglobinemia.

items.label: Recommends primary G-CSF (e.g. pegfilgrastim) every cycle, given age >=65
items.why: Age >=65 on anthracycline-based therapy carries high febrile neutropenia risk that threatens dose intensity.

items.label: Stops ibuprofen/NSAIDs and offers alternative analgesia
items.why: NSAIDs worsen rising creatinine before TLS-risk chemotherapy and interact with methotrexate; pain still needs control.

items.label: Plans for steroid hyperglycemia or adjusts metformin for falling eGFR
items.why: Diabetic on metformin facing high-dose prednisone and AKI: risk of hyperglycemia and metformin accumulation.

items.label: Confirms HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive, so no antiviral prophylaxis needed
items.why: HBV status must be checked before rituximab; here negative serology means no entecavir is required.

items.label: Notes baseline LVEF 60% permits anthracycline
items.why: Normal ejection fraction confirms he can safely receive the doxorubicin in Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP.

items.label: Judges ECOG 2 disease-related, not a reason to de-escalate; honours cure goal
items.why: His decline is from lymphoma and should improve with treatment; he explicitly wants curative therapy.
